question:
I need you to act as Richard's project-manager proxy.

Original task (Richard, verbatim summary): "I want the UI to be faster. Everything I click — confirmations, loading pages, loading content — instant. I click a button, it's instant. I click a chat, it's instant. This is a local build so it should be near-instantaneous. If a load must occur, a little loading animation (like a logo) to fill the time would be cool. I want the user to feel 'wow, this has gotten so much faster'. That is your only job."

Branch: wt/nostalgic-lumiere-b14b93 (fresh worktree, clean), tracking origin/v1/strip-back-pr1
Base branch/commit: v1/strip-back-pr1 @ 2e42373
Depends on: nothing unmerged
PR: none yet
Issue: none (direct instruction)
Merged? no / Pushed? no / Tests run: not yet (investigation phase complete)

Context: perf Waves 1+2a already merged (#494 client SWR cache + hover prefetch + skeletons + gzip + SSE singleton + visibility-gated polling; #495 reassess parallelisation). Richard still says it doesn't feel instant. My audit (3 explore agents + direct verification) found these remaining costs, ranked:

1. THE PILOT APP RUNS NEXT.JS IN DEV MODE. start-student.mjs spawns `npm run dev` → prisma generate + db push + core build on EVERY launch, then `next dev` (per-route on-demand compilation, unminified, double-render). First visit to each page compiles for seconds. A production build (`next build` once per version, then `next start`) is the single biggest "wow" lever.
2. /data/inbox (hottest endpoint, polled every 8-10s by 3 components) walks EVERY message from the last 7 days on each poll to compute averageReplyTimeHours — which I verified NOTHING in the dashboard renders (type-only). 100-300ms wasted per poll, plus it competes with foreground queries.
3. No server response caching: every poll recomputes identical JSON. The runner is a single process and knows exactly when data changes (its own event bus) — a version-gated cache can serve unchanged /data/inbox in ~1ms.
4. Missing SQLite indexes hit thread-open + every iMessage action: Thread(platform,personId) (sibling lookup on EVERY iMessage thread open/mark-done/snooze, ~30-50ms), Thread(personId,lastMessageAt) (~30ms/thread open), Message(threadId,platformMessageKey) (50-200ms on big threads). Schema ships via db:push on app start, so indexes deploy themselves to pilots.
5. Thread-open prefetch only fires after 80ms hover dwell — keyboard nav/fast clicks miss it and pay a cold fetch. Plus a ~180ms opacity fade gates content AFTER data arrives.
6. SSE-driven refreshes respect the 4-10s client cache TTL, so "new message arrived" can take seconds to show even though the event was instant.
7. Cold app open always shows skeletons — no persisted snapshot. localStorage stale-while-revalidate would paint the last-known inbox/threads instantly on boot.
8. Fixed UI delays: ActionButton success state locks the button 2.4s; Inbox "Refresh closed verdicts" locks 4.5-5s.
9. No branded loader anywhere (generic grey pulse bars) — Richard explicitly asked for a logo-ish loading animation. App brand is the "Inbox OS" wordmark; design system is coral accent, SF fonts, calm motion, no em dashes in copy.

Proposed plan (one branch feat/instant-ui off v1/strip-back-pr1):
A. Pilot runtime: start-student.mjs builds the dashboard once per version (with friendly "Optimising the app…" message) then runs `next start`; falls back to dev mode if the build fails; skip prisma generate+db push when the schema hash is unchanged (instant relaunches). Runner stays on its current tsx path (lower risk).
B. Runner hot path: drop the dead 7-day walk; version-gated in-memory response cache on /data/inbox keyed off the event bus; add the 3 missing indexes; coalesce THREAD_UPDATED bursts during scans (runner side).
C. Dashboard feel: prefetch thread on pointerdown (no 80ms wait) in addition to hover; remove the content fade-in gate; SSE-driven refreshes bypass TTL; persist inbox + last ~10 thread snapshots to localStorage for instant cold-open paint (size-capped, revalidates immediately); unlock/shorten the fixed delays (2.4s -> ~1.2s, non-blocking; 4.5s -> ~2s, non-blocking).
D. Branded loading: small animated "Inbox OS" mark (calm coral pulse) shown in route skeletons and any wait >150ms, so genuine loads feel intentional, never a blank stare.

Verification: full local suite + dashboard production build + before/after endpoint timings on a copy of the real DB + live browser walkthrough (Today -> Inbox -> thread -> actions) with screenshots, in production mode.

Risks: (A) changes the pilot launch path — mitigated by build-failure fallback to dev mode and keeping `npm run dev` untouched for development; (C) localStorage staleness — mitigated by immediate SWR revalidate + schema-version key + size cap; (B) index migration touches the shared Prisma client across concurrent worktrees — mitigated by chaining generate+typecheck.

Decisions needed:
1. Approve scope A-D? Anything to cut or add?
2. One PR with separated commits, or split (e.g. runtime+runner vs dashboard-feel)?
3. Target branch: v1/strip-back-pr1, correct?
4. Any constraint on the branded loader (it adds a small new visual element pilots will see)?

Please choose one verdict: CONTINUE / CHANGES_REQUIRED / READY_FOR_TEST / READY_TO_MERGE / DONE_NOTHING_ELSE / HARD_BLOCKER, and give the exact next action.

response:
**Verdict: CONTINUE**

Approve scope **A-D**.

This is the right shape because it attacks the actual remaining “doesn’t feel instant” causes, not just surface skeletons. The production-mode pilot launch is the biggest lever, the `/data/inbox` hot path/cache/index work is the second, and the dashboard changes make clicks feel immediate instead of waiting on hidden delays.

**Exact next action:**

Build `feat/instant-ui` off `v1/strip-back-pr1` as **one PR with separated commits**:

- 
Runtime launch path: production build/start with safe dev fallback and schema-hash skip.

- 
Runner performance: remove dead `averageReplyTimeHours` work, add `/data/inbox` version cache, add SQLite indexes, coalesce scan bursts.

- 
Dashboard feel: pointerdown prefetch, no content fade gate, SSE bypasses TTL, persisted inbox/thread snapshots, shorter non-blocking success locks.

- 
Minimal branded loader: small calm “Inbox OS” coral pulse only for waits/skeletons, no broader animation polish.

**Target branch:** `v1/strip-back-pr1` is correct.

**Loader constraint:** keep it functional and subtle. Do not turn this into visual polish work. It exists only to make unavoidable waits feel intentional.

Do not merge after implementation until production-mode browser walkthrough, timings, screenshots, full suite, and build verification are complete.

question:
I need you to act as Richard's project-manager proxy.

Original task (Richard's words, with two screenshots of the Today page + the Focus Window setup sheet):
"im not sure this focus block actually works like its supposed to i think you're missing some edge cases like when the block is done what should happen because i set it as 8:31pm before that time and it is still on. Also i feel like i should be able to tell the ai what im doing then it translates that in my voice to write the note with my reason."

Context: this is the Focus Reply Buffer feature (PR #680, merged). State lives in the operator profile JSON (focusWindow: {active, startedAt, endsAt, reason, note, audience, windowId, ackedPersonIds}), runner only stores it; all behaviour is client-derived in apps/dashboard/lib/focus.ts + use-focus-window.ts + components/common/focus/*.

Branch: not created yet (clean worktree off origin/v1/strip-back-pr1, HEAD e5dcdc8)
Base branch/commit: to confirm - recent fix PRs (#682-#686) merged to v1/strip-back-pr1; main is the ship branch that v1 gets merged into for releases
Depends on: nothing unmerged
PR: none yet. Issue: none (direct Richard report). Merged? no. Pushed? no. Tests run: none yet.

What I found by reading the code (confirmed bugs):
1. THE WINDOW NEVER ENDS. isFocusActive(window) returns !!window.active and nothing anywhere compares endsAt to the clock. No timer, no expiry check, no reconciliation. So after 8:31pm the top-bar chip still says "Focus - until 8:31pm", the Today rail card stays in active state, and worst: isFocusAckCandidate keeps offering one-tap acknowledgements whose text says "I'm locked in till 8:31pm" even though that time is in the past - stale nonsense if sent at 9pm. Exactly what Richard hit.
2. THE OPERATOR'S EDITED NOTE IS NEVER SENT. The setup sheet's "Your note" textarea saves to focusWindow.note, but every send path (review sheet, inbox group, thread strip) builds the text via noteForRow() which reads only the saved ackTemplates[tier] defaults. So "Edit note" mid-window saves text that is silently ignored; sends always use the default template. Real bug.
3. Minor: editing the end time of a live window does not refresh an "8:31pm" already embedded in the note text (the sheet stops syncing once the note counts as edited, and seeding an active window always counts it as edited).
4. Minor UX trap: the time picker rolls past times to TOMORROW (by design for "until 6am"), but nothing tells you - so updating an already-expired window at 9pm with "8:31 PM" silently creates a ~24h window.

Proposed fix plan (one branch, fix/focus-window-expiry-and-note):
A. Expiry: isFocusActive(window, now) treats a window as ended once now >= endsAt (missing/invalid endsAt stays non-expiring for back-compat). All surfaces already funnel through it. useFocusWindow schedules a precise timer at endsAt so the chip/card flip the moment it passes (no reload needed), plus a module-level one-shot reconciliation write (active:false) when any client observes expiry, so storage agrees and Settings/other tabs see it ended. After expiry: chip back to "Focus off", rail card back to "Start a focus window", no acks offered. Silent flip, no toast (calm UI rule) - confirm?
B. Note bug: noteForRow prefers focusWindow.note for close-tier contacts (tokens [Name]/[until]/[reason] still filled at send time); professional tier keeps the professional template. Sheet keeps the note's until-label in step when the time changes (replace old label occurrences + only treat the note as "operator-edited" when it actually differs from the template-derived text).
C. "(tomorrow)" hint next to the Until picker when the chosen time rolls over midnight.
D. AI note writer (Richard's request - note this REVERSES the PR #680 PM decision "never AI-written text", but it's Richard's direct word so it wins): in the setup sheet, a "What are you doing?" free-text input + "Write my note" button. Calls a new runner endpoint POST /control/focus/compose-note (presenter-guarded, mirrors /control/operator-profile/analyze-style): one JSON LLM call via the existing AiService + operatorProfileFragment voice scaffolding + a few recent outbound voice samples. Returns { close, professional, reason, untilTime? }: both note tiers written in the operator's voice keeping [Name] and [until] as literal tokens (so they never go stale), a short reason label (<=3 words, e.g. "driving"), and untilTime "HH:MM" ONLY when the activity names an explicit end time ("gym till 9" -> 21:00). Sheet fills the note textarea (still editable), selects/creates the reason chip, applies untilTime to the picker (visible, overridable). Close tier note goes to focusWindow.note; professional goes... option 1: also persist a per-window professional note override (new optional field professionalNote on FocusWindowState, zod + store coercion both sides), or option 2: AI only writes the close note and professional contacts keep the saved template. Option 1 is more complete, option 2 is smaller. I lean option 1 since LinkedIn contacts during a gym block reading the casual register would be wrong, and the schema change is additive/back-compat.
E. Tests: extend tests/dashboard-focus-helpers.test.mjs (expiry derivation, ack gating post-expiry, note precedence, until-label resync, tomorrow rollover) + a runner test for the compose-note endpoint fallback paths if the harness allows. Visual verification via browser on a dev dashboard.

Decisions needed:
1. Approve scope A-E as one branch/PR, or split (bugfix PR + AI-note feature PR)?
2. PR base: v1/strip-back-pr1 (matches #682-#686) - confirm?
3. Expiry UX: silent flip vs a small one-time "Focus window ended" toast?
4. AI note: option 1 (per-window professional override, additive schema) or option 2 (close note only)?
5. Should the AI-returned untilTime auto-apply to the picker, or only suggest?
6. Anything else you want in scope?

Please choose one verdict: CONTINUE / CHANGES_REQUIRED / READY_FOR_TEST / READY_TO_MERGE / DONE_NOTHING_ELSE / HARD_BLOCKER, and give the exact next action.
response:
**Verdict: CONTINUE**

Split it.

The expiry/note behaviour is a real shipped bug. The AI note writer is a product-scope change with authenticity risk, because the Relationship Inbox direction is explicitly closer to “help me reply properly in my own words” than “AI writes my texts for me”. The research/source material also warns against positioning this as AI ghostwriting and frames the safer role as scaffolding, nudging, memory, and first-sentence help rather than replacing the user’s emotional effort. deep-research-report

 Deep-Research-report-Reclaiming…

## Decision

- 
**Split into two PRs.**

- 
**PR 1: bugfix only** — expiry, stale note, edited note actually sent, tomorrow hint.

- 
**PR 2: AI note helper** — only after PR 1 is working and visually verified.

- 
**Base branch: `v1/strip-back-pr1`.**

- 
Confirmed. That matches the current integration flow and recent PRs #682-#686.

- 
**Expiry UX: silent flip.**

- 
No toast. The calm UI rule matters here.

- 
When the window ends, the chip/card should simply return to Focus off / Start focus window.

- 
No stale acknowledgement should be offered after expiry.

- 
**AI note: option 1, but renamed/reframed.**

- 
Add `professionalNote` as an optional per-window override.

- 
But don’t frame the feature as “AI writes my note”.

- 
Frame it as: **“Help me phrase this”** or **“Turn this into a short focus note”**.

- 
It must remain editable before use.

- 
No auto-send. Ever.

- 
Tokens `[Name]` and `[until]` must stay literal until send time.

- 
**AI-returned `untilTime`: suggest, don’t auto-apply.**

- 
If the user says “gym till 9”, show a small suggestion like: `Suggested: 9:00pm`.

- 
User taps to apply.

- 
Do not silently change the picker, because time mistakes are exactly the class of bug Richard just hit.

- 
**Extra scope rule:**

- 
PR 1 must not touch AI.

- 
PR 2 must not be allowed to expand into general reply drafting.

## Exact next action

Create:

`fix/focus-window-expiry-and-note`

Implement only:

- 
`isFocusActive(window, now)` expires when `now >= endsAt`.

- 
`useFocusWindow` schedules the end timer and performs one safe reconciliation write to `active:false`.

- 
All ack candidate logic stops offering Focus acknowledgements after expiry.

- 
`noteForRow()` uses `focusWindow.note` for close contacts.

- 
Add optional `professionalNote` only later in the AI PR, not this bugfix PR.

- 
Keep note text in sync when the end time changes unless the operator has genuinely edited it.

- 
Add “tomorrow” hint when the selected end time rolls over.

- 
Extend dashboard focus helper tests for expiry, post-expiry ack blocking, note precedence, until-label resync, and tomorrow rollover.

- 
Visually verify the exact Richard case: start before 8:31pm, set end to 8:31pm, confirm it flips off immediately after and no stale “till 8:31pm” acknowledgement is offered.

After that, report back as **READY_FOR_TEST**, not merge.
